text:
jamie: Heads up — I pushed a tiny PR to normalize the sample audit-log JSON we show in the export docs. The root keys were inconsistent (event_time vs timestamp) and customers complained it makes parsing examples annoying. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/987
priya: Thanks for doing that. Can you also add a short note about redaction placeholders? Legal asked that we show the pseudonymized fields in examples, not full PII.
jamie: Yep — added a 1-line comment above the sample and a quick example of a pseudonymized username. Also switched event_time -> iso_timestamp everywhere.
mike: Quick check — does the sample still match the SDK export payload? We need the curl example in the docs to be copy-pastable.
jamie: Good point. I updated the curl snippet to use the SDK export format (payload has "records" array). Also added a header example for retention TTL: `X-Redwood-Retention-TTL: 90d` so folks see how to request shorter retention on export.
priya: Can you paste the snippet here so I can sanity-check wording for SOC2-friendly phrasing? Legal wants us to avoid promising retention enforcement on behalf of customers.
jie (docs-bot): Automated check: PR 987 failed linkcheck for one anchor `#export-format` in export.md
jamie: Ah — broken anchor. I fixed the anchor name in export.md, and updated the link in the sidebar. Also updated the example text to say "include optional retention header; customers must confirm enforcement on their storage side" (per legal) 
priya: Looks good. One nit: replace "pseudonymized_username" with "user_id_pseudonym" to discourage copying real emails.
mike: Also add a short note about time fields: "All timestamps in examples are ISO 8601 UTC" — saves confusion between epoch vs iso.
jamie: Added both changes. Here's the final sample block I added to the doc for review:
```json
{
  "export_id": "exp_01F...",
  "iso_timestamp": "2026-03-20T18:24:12Z",
  "records": [
    {
      "event": "api.request",
      "user_id_pseudonym": "pseud_82a3",
      "resource": "/v1/generate",
      "meta": { "model": "redwood-instruct-1" }
    }
  ]
}
```
priya: That looks perfect. Can you also add a one-liner under the sample: "Note: sample shows pseudonymized identifiers; do not store unredacted PII in exported artifacts."
jamie: Done. I also added an inline example curl command showing the retention header and Content-Type, e.g.:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Redwood-Retention-TTL: 90d" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export" -d '{"start":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z","end":"2026-03-20T23:59:59Z"}'
```
mike: Awesome. One last request from security: include a short note about rotating the export presigned URL in <=24h if you link to S3.
jamie: Added a sentence: "If export creates a presigned storage URL, rotate or invalidate links within 24 hours and document the lifecycle in your retention policy."
priya: LGTM. I'll add a tiny docs-review label and merge this afternoon once CI passes. :thumbsup:
jamie: Thanks — I'll watch CI and address any remaining nit fixes.
docs-bot: CI passed for PR 987 — linkcheck ok, markdown lint ok, deploy-preview up at https://deploy-preview-987--docs.redwood.ai/exports.html :rocket:
